findings.claim: The closer scan now treats any later line starting with a fence as an unclosed-block error, but the new opener check only strips spaces, not tabs. A tab-indented fence is neither an opener nor a closer here. Markdown allows at most 3 leading spaces for a fence, yet TrimLeft accepts any number of spaces, so a 4+ space indented line (an indented code block) is treated as a fence. This is a minor parser looseness in a test helper.

The new headroom test asserts the body is at most 690 estimated tokens, a threshold tied to the current wording. The added `L<n>` clause and `memorycard` word in the body consume headroom, so future legitimate edits to the Hard Rules will fail this test with a token-count message rather than a behavioral one. The check is brittle but intentional.

evidence: Reviewed all six changed paths in the diff.
The SKILL.md wording changes match the strings asserted by the updated tests (`L<n>` is its shaper Log entry; commit `-` until the task is committed; memorycard mirror `odd/<feature>/tasks`).
The overview sentence was moved to references/format.md and the new test asserts it is present there.
The chain-entry closer logic returns the first exact fence line and errors on another opening fence, with tests covering the indented, unclosed-then-text, and indented-second-block cases.
